# The `{webexercises}` package

<img src="man/figures/logo.png" style="float:right; max-width:280px; width: 25%;" />

The goal of `{webexercises}` is to enable instructors to easily create interactive web pages that students can use in self-guided learning. Although `{webexercises}` has fewer features than RStudio's [learnr](https://rstudio.github.io/learnr/) package, it is more lightweight: whereas `{learnr}` tutorials must be either hosted on a shiny server or run locally, `{webexercises}` creates standalone HTML files that require only a JavaScript-enabled browser. It is also extremely simple to use. See the [webexercises website](https://psyteachr.github.io/webexercises/) for demos and instructions.

## Installation

You can install `{webexercises}` from CRAN using:

```{r install-cran, eval=FALSE}
install.packages("webexercises")
```

You can install the development version from [GitHub](https://github.com/PsyTeachR/webexercises) with:

```{r install-webexercises, eval=FALSE}
devtools::install_github("psyteachr/webexercises")
```

## This fork

`BriceNocenti/webexercises` is a thin fork of `PsyTeachR/webexercises`. It adds:

- **a Quarto extension.** Install it once, name the filter, and `webex.css` / `webex.js` arrive as
  an HTML dependency on every HTML page -- a document, a chapter of a book, a page of a website,
  all the same, with no `css:` line and no relative path to resolve:

  ``` bash
  quarto add BriceNocenti/webexercises
  ```

  ``` yaml
  filters: [webexercises]
  ```

  `add_to_quarto()` does both steps from R, and `create_quarto_doc()` starts a document that way.

- **`webexercises_default2()`**, an R Markdown format built on `bookdown::html_document2()` so that
  cross-references work. Retained for documents that have not moved to Quarto.
- **`textbox()`**, a free-text answer box, and checkbox `longmcq()` for questions with several
  right answers.
- **the submit / try-again cycle**: a `::: {.webex-check}` section grows a button that grades every
  widget inside it, tells the reader how many are right, and can be reset. Its three strings follow
  the document's `lang:` -- `:root:lang(fr)` gives the French ones, with no stylesheet to override.
- **a dark page.** Four colour literals became variables keeping the literal as their fallback, and
  the fills are derived from the stylesheet's own semantic colours with `color-mix()`, so the
  widgets follow a light/dark switch without a theme and with no new colour.

⚠ **`webex.js` is plain JavaScript.** The `<script>` wrapper an `after_body` include needs is added
at render time by `webex_after_body()`; an HTML dependency takes the file itself.
